A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LitePT, with matching authors, architecture, and principal experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original LitePT segmentation and detection results, efficiency measurements, and architectural ablations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results and adds positional-encoding comparisons, cross-dataset transfer, ModelNet40 classification, PointMamba comparisons, and further scaling and efficiency measurements.

M1.justification: The stage-specific convolution/attention architecture, PointROPE construction, model variants, decoder designs, and losses remain unchanged. Equations 1–4 and Appendix A describe the same method; the additional evaluations do not document a redesign of LitePT.

E1.justification: V2 adds ModelNet40 object classification, extending the original segmentation/detection task coverage. It also adds a distinct transfer scenario from synthetic Structured3D training to ScanNet evaluation with frozen encoders. The original datasets and tasks are retained.

E2.justification: V2 adds PointMamba comparisons for classification, ScanNet segmentation, and computational scaling, and introduces sinusoidal APE and RPE alternatives in the positional-encoding comparison. These are focused comparator additions; the original main benchmark comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include Structured3D pretraining followed by frozen-encoder, multiscale linear probing on ScanNet; classification trained from scratch without voting; and PointMamba evaluation with a fixed token-to-input ratio and a 640-token ScanNet configuration. These materially extend evaluation design. Existing training settings in Tables 13–15 are unchanged.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained ablations, v2 tests alternative positional encodings, transfer under dataset shift, and memory/latency sensitivity to input point count against PointMamba (Appendix C.1–C.3 and Figure 9). The original coordinate-system and axis-allocation ablations remain, and the chunking/TTA analysis moves from C.2 to C.6 without changing its findings.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, or reports confidence intervals, run-to-run variability, or significance tests. Dataset-averaged efficiency measurements already appear in v1; the new results do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Original numerical results are retained, while substantial new entries appear. Table 18 reports transfer mIoU of 65.0 for LitePT-S versus 57.1 for PTv3. Table 19 reports ModelNet40 accuracy of 92.5 versus PointMamba's 92.4 and ScanNet mIoU of 76.5 versus 60.5. New LitePT-L results include 74.0 Waymo mIoU, 82.6 nuScenes mIoU, and 42.3 ScanNet instance mAP. Positional-encoding and outdoor-efficiency results are also added. LitePT-L's Structured3D score of 85.4 was already reported in v1.

T1.justification: The stage-selection equations and axis-wise PointROPE definitions are mathematically unchanged. Neither version supplies additional theorems or proofs; the new generalization and scaling explanations are empirical interpretations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: stage-tailored convolution and attention with parameter-free PointROPE, offering favorable accuracy and efficiency against PTv3. Replacing 'training-free' with 'parameter-free' in the abstract aligns terminology with an already stated property rather than introducing a new contribution.

C2.justification: New appendix discussion attributes transfer performance to PointROPE's relative geometry, explains PointMamba's scaling limitations through sampling and feature propagation, and relates larger-model gains to data volume. These are localized additions to interpretation and applicability boundaries; the original convolution/attention explanation and future-work discussion remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 supplies benchmark-specific details, including PointMamba's 640-token configuration and RTX 4090 constraint, and hardware/AMP settings for Waymo timing. Qualitative captions newly identify validation-set examples. Existing architecture and training specifications, the CUDA implementation statement, and code/model access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The hybrid-model discussion adds CoAtNet, DyCo3D, Mask3D, and PVTSSD, acknowledging bottleneck Transformers and task-specific Transformer decoders alongside uniform hybrid blocks. PointMamba is also newly cited and compared. This refines positioning without replacing the paper's central distinction; publication-metadata updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized abstract and related-work edits, standardizes PointROPE and nuScenes terminology, corrects wording, and expands acknowledgments. Appendix C gains subsections and relocates the existing chunking/TTA discussion, while the main narrative and section organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The appendix substantially expands its comparative displays with Tables 17–21 covering encoding alternatives, transfer, PointMamba, model scaling, and outdoor efficiency, plus Figure 9's memory/latency curves. Existing main displays are retained. The old TTA table becomes Table 22, and the unchanged qualitative images become Figures 10–15 with clarified captions.

improvement.justification: V1 already provides broad evidence for the central architecture and efficiency claims. V2 strengthens validation through alternative positional encodings, transfer, PointMamba comparisons, and outdoor timing, while improving related-work coverage. The gain is limited by sparse details for some new protocols and interpretations that do not isolate PointROPE or data volume as causal factors. Overall, the additions provide useful supporting evidence without changing the established core.
